title: Make word frequency counting Unicode-aware with stable tie order
prompt:
topWords() in src/wordfreq.mjs only understands ASCII and its ordering is wrong for our multilingual support tickets. Rework it to this spec:

- topWords(text, n, { stopWords }) returns [word, count] pairs. n omitted/undefined means all words.
- A word is a maximal run of Unicode letters, combining marks and digits. A single apostrophe (' or ’) or hyphen BETWEEN two such characters joins them into one word ("don't", "e-mail", "rock'n'roll"); apostrophes/hyphens at the edges or doubled ("--") are separators.
- Words are normalised before counting: Unicode NFC, then lower-case, and ’ becomes '. So "École", "école" and the decomposed "e\u0301cole" are the same word, and "Don’t" equals "don't".
- stopWords are normalised the same way and excluded.
- Order: higher count first; ties keep the order in which the words first appeared in the text.

Run `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`.
